items.stem: Define the term 'income statement'.
items.answer: A financial statement showing a business's revenue, costs and profit (or loss) over a period of time, usually one year.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, a financial statement showing a business's revenue, costs and profit (or loss) over a period of time, usually one year. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between gross profit and operating profit.
items.answer: Gross profit is revenue minus cost of sales; operating profit also deducts overhead expenses such as rent, salaries and marketing.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each. [2]

items.stem: Explain why the quality of profit matters as well as the amount.
items.answer: Profit from one-off events (e.g. selling assets) cannot be repeated; high-quality profit comes from continuing trading and is sustainable.
items.markingKey: 1 mark one-off v recurring; 1 mark sustainability. [2]

items.stem: Occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby. Desert Bloom Hotels plc, a public limited company in the United Arab Emirates with about 3,100 employees, operates fourteen four- and five-star hotels. Explain what Desert Bloom's income statement could tell its managers and shareholders.
items.answer: Points to develop for Desert Bloom: the income statement shows revenue, costs and profit over a period; gross and operating profit margins show efficiency; trends over years reveal performance; profit for the year shows funds for dividends and reinvestment.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: the income statement shows revenue, costs and profit over a period. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Desert Bloom: hospitality, about 3,100 employees, public limited company in the United Arab Emirates; occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Desert Bloom, e.g. gross and operating profit margins show efficiency; trends over years reveal performance; profit for the year shows funds for dividends and reinvestment. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Nusantara Apparel Tbk is a public limited company based in Jakarta, Indonesia. It makes sportswear under contract for global brands and employs about 4,000 people. A global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours. Explain why Nusantara Apparel's operating profit might fall even though its gross profit has risen.
items.answer: Points to develop for Nusantara Apparel: operating profit = gross profit − overheads; rising overheads (rent, salaries, marketing); expansion costs before revenue grows; one-off expenses such as restructuring.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: operating profit = gross profit − overheads. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Nusantara Apparel: clothing manufacturing, about 4,000 employees, public limited company in Indonesia; a global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Nusantara Apparel, e.g. rising overheads (rent, salaries, marketing); expansion costs before revenue grows; one-off expenses such as restructuring. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Desert Bloom Hotels plc is a public limited company based in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates. It operates fourteen four- and five-star hotels and employs about 3,100 people. Occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby. Discuss the usefulness of the income statement in judging the performance of Desert Bloom.
items.answer: For: shows profitability and margins; trends over time; comparisons with rivals. Against: profit is not cash; historic data; ignores non-financial performance. Judgement: the decision for Desert Bloom depends mainly on the quality of profit, and also on the use of other statements.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Desert Bloom: hospitality, about 3,100 employees, public limited company in the United Arab Emirates; occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. shows profitability and margins; trends over time; comparisons with rivals; arguments against, e.g. profit is not cash; historic data; ignores non-financial performance. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the quality of profit; the use of other statements; comparability of data. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Desert Bloom, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Which item is deducted from gross profit to calculate operating profit?
items.answer: Overhead (operating) expenses
items.markingKey: Overhead (operating) expenses. Operating profit = gross profit − operating expenses.

items.stem: Based in Santiago, Andina Solar SpA (private limited company) designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes. The business has around 380 employees. The government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy. Explain one disadvantage to Andina Solar of retaining most of its profit for the year rather than paying dividends.
items.answer: Shareholders may be dissatisfied.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. shareholders may be dissatisfied; share price may fall; opportunity cost of the funds. 1 mark: explained in the context of Andina Solar (renewable energy). [2]

items.stem: Explain two ways a business could increase its gross profit margin.
items.answer: Raise selling prices (if demand is inelastic) or reduce cost of sales, e.g. by negotiating with suppliers, cutting waste or switching to cheaper materials.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark method, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Extracts from the latest income statement of Bosphorus Home AŞ ($m): revenue 20; cost of sales 12; overhead expenses 4. Calculate the gross profit and the operating profit.
items.answer: Gross profit $8m; operating profit $4m

items.answer: Points to develop for Gold Coast Cocoa: the income statement shows revenue, costs and profit over a period; gross and operating profit margins show efficiency; trends over years reveal performance; profit for the year shows funds for dividends and reinvestment.

items.stem: Lagos Bites Ltd is a private limited company based in Lagos, Nigeria. It produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin and employs about 700 people. Rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins. (a) Define 'retained earnings'. (b) Explain one advantage to Lagos Bites of retaining most of its profit for the year rather than paying dividends.
items.answer: (a) The part of profit for the year that is kept in the business rather than paid out as dividends. (b) Internal finance for investment with no interest.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (internal finance for investment with no interest; no dilution of ownership; strengthens the statement of financial position), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Lagos Bites [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'statement of financial position'.
items.answer: A financial statement showing the value of a business's assets, liabilities and equity at a particular date.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, a financial statement showing the value of a business's assets, liabilities and equity at a particular date. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business needs enough working capital.
items.answer: It must pay suppliers, wages and other short-term debts as they fall due; too little working capital risks insolvency even if profitable.
items.markingKey: 1 mark meets short-term obligations; 1 mark consequence of shortage. [2]

items.stem: Explain why the value of non-current assets on the statement of financial position may differ from their market value.
items.answer: They are recorded at historical cost less depreciation, which may not reflect what they could be sold for; intangible assets such as brands may not be shown.
items.markingKey: 1 mark historical cost/depreciation; 1 mark market value or intangibles. [2]

items.stem: The central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps. BatikPay Sdn Bhd, a private limited company in Malaysia with about 210 employees, runs a mobile payments app used by 4 million customers and 90 000 small shops. Explain the possible consequences for BatikPay of having too little working capital.
items.answer: Points to develop for BatikPay: working capital = current assets − current liabilities; difficulty paying suppliers and wages; loss of supplier credit and discounts; risk of insolvency even when profitable.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: working capital = current assets − current liabilities. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (BatikPay: financial technology, about 210 employees, private limited company in Malaysia; the central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for BatikPay, e.g. difficulty paying suppliers and wages; loss of supplier credit and discounts; risk of insolvency even when profitable. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd is a private limited company based in Accra, Ghana. It buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars and employs about 450 people. World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Evaluate the best way for Gold Coast Cocoa to improve its working capital position.
items.answer: For: reduce inventory (JIT); collect receivables faster; negotiate longer credit from suppliers. Against: lower inventory risks stock-outs; tight credit may lose customers; suppliers may refuse. Judgement: the decision for Gold Coast Cocoa depends mainly on the cause of the shortage, and also on its relationship with suppliers and customers.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Gold Coast Cocoa: confectionery, about 450 employees, private limited company in Ghana; world cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. reduce inventory (JIT); collect receivables faster; negotiate longer credit from suppliers; arguments against, e.g. lower inventory risks stock-outs; tight credit may lose customers; suppliers may refuse. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the cause of the shortage; its relationship with suppliers and customers; how quickly cash is needed. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Gold Coast Cocoa, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Which business term is described here: "Debts the business must repay within one year, such as trade payables, overdrafts and tax owed."
items.answer: current liabilities
items.markingKey: This is the definition of current liabilities.

items.stem: Based in Madrid, Iberia Moda SA (public limited company) runs 180 fast-fashion clothing stores and an online shop. The business has around 6,000 employees. Online sales are growing quickly while sales in its high-street stores are falling. Explain one disadvantage to Iberia Moda of selling and leasing back its premises to raise cash.
items.answer: Loses ownership of a valuable asset.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. loses ownership of a valuable asset; ongoing lease payments reduce profit; loses gains from rising property values. 1 mark: explained in the context of Iberia Moda (clothing retail). [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between current liabilities and non-current liabilities.
items.answer: Current liabilities must be paid within a year (e.g. trade payables, overdraft); non-current liabilities are due after more than a year (e.g. long-term loans).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each. [2]

items.stem: A business has current assets of $3.25m and current liabilities of $1.62m. What is its working capital?

Extracts from the statement of financial position of Bosphorus Home AŞ ($m): non-current assets 10; inventory 2.4; trade receivables 1; cash 0.4; current liabilities 3.04; non-current liabilities 2. Calculate the working capital.
items.answer: Working capital $0.76m
items.markingKey: Current assets = 2.4 + 1 + 0.4 = 3.8 [1]; working capital = 3.8 − 3.04 = 0.76 [1]. [2]

items.stem: Extracts from the statement of financial position of Indus Sports Goods Ltd ($m): non-current assets 10; inventory 0.8; trade receivables 1.8; cash 0.8; current liabilities 3.4; non-current liabilities 3. Calculate the working capital and the total equity.
items.answer: Working capital $0m; equity $7m
items.markingKey: Current assets = 0.8 + 1.8 + 0.8 = 3.4 [1]; working capital = 3.4 − 3.4 = 0 [1]; total assets = 13.4; total liabilities = 6.4; equity = 7 [1]. [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'depreciation'.
items.answer: The fall in the value of a non-current asset over its useful life, recorded as an expense in the income statement each year.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the fall in the value of a non-current asset over its useful life, recorded as an expense in the income statement each year. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why businesses depreciate non-current assets.
items.answer: To match the cost of an asset to the years in which it helps earn revenue, so profit is not overstated, and to show a realistic asset value.
items.markingKey: 1 mark matching/accurate profit; 1 mark realistic asset value. [2]

items.stem: Explain how overvaluing inventory affects the financial statements.
items.answer: Closing inventory too high reduces cost of sales, so gross and operating profit are overstated, and current assets on the SFP are overstated.
items.markingKey: 1 mark profit overstated; 1 mark assets overstated. [2]

items.stem: Lagos Bites Ltd is a private limited company based in Lagos, Nigeria. It produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin and employs about 700 people. Rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins. Explain why Lagos Bites must value its inventory carefully.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lagos Bites: inventory valued at lower of cost and NRV; affects cost of sales and profit; affects current assets and liquidity ratios; obsolete or damaged stock must be written down.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: inventory valued at lower of cost and NRV. items.answer: Points to develop for Gold Coast Cocoa: depreciation is a non-cash expense; higher depreciation lowers operating profit; net book value of assets falls faster; affects ratios such as ROCE and gearing.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: depreciation is a non-cash expense. items.stem: Inventory should be valued in the accounts at
options: the lower of cost and net realisable value
the higher of cost and selling price
its replacement cost in every case
items.answer: the lower of cost and net realisable value
items.markingKey: the lower of cost and net realisable value. Prudence: inventory is not valued above what it can be sold for.

items.answer: Lower reported profit in early years.

items.stem: Explain why depreciation is not a cash flow.
items.answer: The cash leaves when the asset is bought; depreciation only allocates that cost over time in the accounts, so no money is paid each year.
items.markingKey: 1 mark cash paid at purchase; 1 mark accounting allocation. [2]

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'profit for the year'?
options: The amount for which inventory could be sold, minus any costs of making it ready for sale and selling it.
Assets the business expects to keep and use for more than one year, such as buildings, machinery and vehicles.
The profit remaining after interest (finance costs) and corporation tax have been deducted from operating profit; it is available for dividends and retained earnings.
items.answer: The profit remaining after interest (finance costs) and corporation tax have been deducted from operating profit; it is available for dividends and retained earnings.
items.markingKey: profit for the year: The profit remaining after interest (finance costs) and corporation tax have been deducted from operating profit; it is available for dividends and retained earnings.

items.stem: Based in Karachi, Indus Sports Goods Ltd (private limited company) makes hand-stitched and machine-stitched footballs and cricket equipment. The business has around 950 employees. items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'current liabilities'?
options: The fall in the value of a non-current asset over its useful life, recorded as an expense in the income statement each year.
A financial statement showing the value of a business's assets, liabilities and equity at a particular date.
Debts the business must repay within one year, such as trade payables, overdrafts and tax owed.
The amount for which inventory could be sold, minus any costs of making it ready for sale and selling it.
items.answer: Debts the business must repay within one year, such as trade payables, overdrafts and tax owed.
items.markingKey: current liabilities: Debts the business must repay within one year, such as trade payables, overdrafts and tax owed.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain why a business needs enough working capital. (b) Explain the difference between current liabilities and non-current liabilities.
items.answer: (a) It must pay suppliers, wages and other short-term debts as they fall due; too little working capital risks insolvency even if profitable. (b) Current liabilities must be paid within a year (e.g. trade payables, overdraft); non-current liabilities are due after more than a year (e.g. long-term loans).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark meets short-term obligations; 1 mark consequence of shortage. [2] (b) 1 mark each. [2]
